title: God of Our Fathers, 'Tis Thy Hand
description: God of Our Fathers, 'Tis Thy Hand in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 791 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Temperance Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God of our fa-thers, 'tis thy hand Hath turned the tide of death a-way, That rolled in mad-ness o'er the land, And filled thy peo-ple with dis-may.

lines: God of our fathers, 'tis thy hand
Hath turned the tide of death away,
That rolled in madness o'er the land,
And filled thy people with dismay.
Thy voice awaked us from our dream:
Thy spirit taught our hearts to feel;
'Twas thy own light, whose radiant beam
Came down our duty to reveal.
Our spirits trust for strength divine;
Gird us with heaven's own energy,
And o'er our paths let wisdom shine.
The work of man's destruction stay;
The tide of fire still backward press;
